title: Individual, Dictator, and Democratic punishment in public good games with perfect and imperfect observability
abstract: FLAG: Could not retrieve verbatim abstract from IDEAS for this paper (RePEc handle eee/pubeco/v178y2019). Based on publisher descriptions and the working-paper version: the study experimentally compares democratic punishment (where group members decide by majority vote whether to inflict punishment) with individual peer-to-peer and dictatorial punishment in repeated public-good contribution games, under both perfect and imperfect monitoring of contributions. Findings: in conditions without noise, cooperation and payoffs are higher when more consensus is required for punishment; under noise, cooperation is lower when more consensus is required.
